subject.title: Telegram: Auto-reply to unauthorized group senders with admin contact instructions

question: Should Telegram add an opt-in auto-reply for group senders denied by `groupAllowFrom`/`groupPolicy`, and what default, cooldown, raw-ID, and admin-contact semantics should it use?
rationale: The request changes a silent authorization denial into visible group output and likely adds config surface, so automation cannot safely choose the security/privacy contract.

options.title: Add Opt-In Rate-Limited Notice
options.body: Add a Telegram plugin setting for denied-sender onboarding replies with per-chat/topic/sender cooldown, configurable admin-contact wording, and explicit raw-ID disclosure rules.

options.title: Use Operator Audit Instead
options.body: Keep unauthorized senders silent and satisfy the visibility need through owner notification or denied-inbound audit work such as https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/77546.

options.title: Keep Silent Denial
options.body: Decline sender-facing replies for now and keep logs, docs, and manual Telegram ID discovery as the supported posture.

recommendation.title: Add Opt-In Rate-Limited Notice
recommendation.body: Add a Telegram plugin setting for denied-sender onboarding replies with per-chat/topic/sender cooldown, configurable admin-contact wording, and explicit raw-ID disclosure rules.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest sampled ownership signal for the Telegram authorization UX and adjacent docs/runtime surface.
